title: Climate Activist William Lawrence Wins Michigan's Pivotal Battleground House Primary
excerpt: The Sunrise Movement co-founder defeated two moderate candidates in a three-way Democratic primary for Michigan's 7th District, setting up a high-stakes November contest against Republican Rep. Tom Barrett.
body:
• William Lawrence, 35, co-founder of the Sunrise Movement, won the Democratic primary in Michigan's 7th Congressional District on Tuesday
  • Lawrence defeated former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Bridget Brink and Navy SEAL veteran Matt Maasdam, who split the moderate vote
  • The progressive activist will face Republican Rep. Tom Barrett in November in one of the most competitive House races in the country
  • The victory extends a string of progressive primary wins that have reshaped the Democratic Party ahead of the 2026 midterms

William Lawrence, a 35-year-old community organizer and co-founder of the Sunrise Movement climate activist group, won the Democratic primary in Michigan's 7th Congressional District on Tuesday night, according to projections by Decision Desk HQ, NBC News, the Associated Press, and CNN.

Lawrence defeated two more moderate opponents — former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Bridget Brink and Navy SEAL veteran Matt Maasdam — in what had become one of the most closely watched House primaries in the country. He will now face first-term Republican Rep. Tom Barrett in November in a district widely considered a tossup.

A Split Moderate Vote Cleared the Path

The result underscored how Lawrence, initially considered an underdog, benefited from the moderate lane being divided. Brink, a career diplomat who broke with President Donald Trump over Ukraine policy, had consolidated much of the Democratic establishment's support. Maasdam, who served as a military aide to former President Barack Obama, was backed by Sen. Elissa Slotkin, who previously represented the district before winning her Senate race in 2024.

But with both candidates competing for the same pool of centrist voters, Lawrence held the progressive base to himself. He was endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, Rep. Rashida Tlaib of Michigan, and Rep. Ro Khanna of California.

"Tonight the people of Michigan's 7th District sent a clear message: they are tired of Silicon Valley billionaires and D.C. insiders determining the future of our towns and our country."

— William Lawrence, in his victory statement

A Controversial Campaign

Lawrence's path to the nomination was not without turbulence. His campaign drew sharp criticism from the Congressional Black Caucus and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries after the Huffington Post reported on 2024 podcast remarks in which Lawrence said Black political leaders "defang the White left." Lawrence apologized for the comments, but they became a significant flashpoint in the primary.

Despite the controversy, Lawrence's grassroots operation proved formidable. Born and raised in East Lansing, he graduated from Swarthmore College before co-founding the Sunrise Movement, which has become one of the most influential climate advocacy organizations in American politics. He also worked as a community organizer helping low-income families avoid homelessness in mid-Michigan.

What It Means for November

The 7th District, centered around Lansing and stretching across several mid-Michigan counties, is considered one of Democrats' best pickup opportunities as they seek to reclaim their House majority. Barrett, an Army veteran and helicopter pilot, flipped the district for Republicans in 2024 by nearly four percentage points.

Republicans wasted no time framing the general election. "Army veteran and helicopter pilot Tom Barrett is a proven fighter for mid-Michigan," said Zach Bannon, a spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Committee, calling Lawrence a "socialist" who is "too extreme" for the district.

The Cook Political Report and Inside Elections both rate the race as a tossup, making it one of the most consequential House contests of the 2026 cycle.

Part of a Broader Progressive Wave

Lawrence's victory is the latest in a series of progressive wins that have reshaped the Democratic Party in 2026. In June, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's endorsed slate swept three congressional primaries, with democratic socialists Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez unseating establishment-backed candidates. In Colorado, Melat Kiros defeated 30-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette.

Indian American Rep. Ro Khanna, who endorsed Lawrence, has been a prominent voice in the progressive wing's push to center economic populism over cultural issues — a strategy that appears to be resonating with primary voters across the country. The broader movement's emphasis on housing affordability, climate action, and income inequality has drawn support from diverse coalitions, including South Asian American organizers active in groups like the Sunrise Movement and the Democratic Socialists of America.

But whether that formula can translate to a general election in a swing district remains the central question. As CNN's analysis noted, the race sets up "a rare test of a Sanders-backed, left-wing candidate in a swing race." For Democrats counting on Michigan's 7th to flip, November will be the proving ground.
